To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have found a record of NAO in the Iberia Range, and that we have extended the record of NAO back to AD 1000.
the isotopic composition (δ18O and δC) of authigenic carbonate in Lagunillo sediment records the precipitation/evapotranspiration ratio and that this record can be used as a proxy for the NAO.
the Lagunillo del Tajo sedimentary record provides a proxy of past precipitation variability and the NAO index in the Iberia Peninsula.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the reconstruction of the North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO) from the last millennium, using the oxygen (δ18O and δ2H) and carbon (Δ14C, δ13C and δ15N) isotope composition of authigenic carbonate from a lake sediment in the Iberic Range, Spain (Lagunillo del Tej).
the use of the Lagunillo del Téjo lake as a proxy for the reconstruction of precipitation variability in the Iberia Range during the last millennium.
the use of carbonate δ18O to reconstruct past climate variability and to understand the mechanisms controlling the hydrology of a sensitive mountain lake.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the isotopic composition and carbonate content of the sedimentary sequence of Lagunillo del tejo lake are strongly related to the North Atlantic Oscillation.
the NAO index has a strong impact on climate variability and precipitation patterns, and therefore on the hydrological cycle of this region.

the Lagunillo del tejo record shows a strong correspondence between the NAO and the δ18O and the δ13C of the carbonate, and therefore, the δ18O of the carbonate can be considered as an indicator of the NAO index.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Lagunillo del Tajo lake is a sensitive recorder of precipitation variability in the Iberia, which has been strongly controlled by the North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO).

the NAO is the most important climatic factor in the Iberia Peninsula, especially in the Iberic Range, and that the isotopic signature of Lagunillo del Tajo can be used as a proxy to infer NAO variability in the past.
the isotopic composition and the stable isotopes of water are good indicators to study the climate change in the last millennium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the isotopic signature of carbonate in Lagunillo is a proxy for precipitation variability, and therefore a proxy of NAO.
the Lagunillo del Tajo lake system is a sensitive site for climate change studies and that the carbonate δ18O record is a proxy that reflects NAO variability.
the Lagunillo del tejo site is a good proxy for the NAO and that the δ18O of authigenic carbonate can be used to infer past NAO variability.
